one-check-per-line.why: all 6 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 6

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file name"

words-only.why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 2 to 6 stay within their words. For example, Check 3's "stdout still contains the bad-row lines" follows from "other files still checked and reported", and the usage-message and read-before-check tests are correctly listed under Advisory. Check 1 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition requires that "A file named twice is reported twice", and its test run names `$T/bad.jsonl` twice. The expect line says nothing about duplicate arguments. "Checks every file named in order" does not force a duplicate to be reported twice, so this is an edge-case test the words don't require. It belongs under Advisory. Check 1 also fixes the single-file output to `$T/bad.jsonl:2: <JSON.parse message>`. That ties the result to one error source, which is stricter than "as for one file before".

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository facts. Every file they name is tracked: packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, src/index.js, test/cli.test.js, README.md and .github/workflows/test.yml. `npm test` at the root and `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint` match the scripts. The root script already uses `--workspaces`, so the workspace flag fits. The shell syntax is valid: `T=$(mktemp -d)`, `printf '{oops}\n' | B $T/a.jsonl -`, `printf '{}\n' | B - -; echo $?`, and `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` used with `git diff ..HEAD -- path`. `gh pr view <pr> --repo ... --json body,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` uses real gh flags and fields. The JavaScript is valid: `readFileSync(0, 'utf8')`, `process.argv.slice(2)` and spawnSync with `input`. The verifier defines the shorthand B as the node command before it uses it. `<pr>` and `<merge-base>` are placeholders, and the brief says how to fill them. I found no command that would fail as written.

catches-traps.why: All four must_catch items are handled. (1) Check 3 runs `B $T/a.jsonl $T/missing.jsonl $T/bad.jsonl` together and requires exit 2, an error on stderr, and stdout that "still contains the bad-row lines for `$T/bad.jsonl`". (2) Check 4 runs `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`, with an empty diff as the clear pass. That compares the PR head with the base. (3) Builder step 4: "Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md" with the usage line, `-` for stdin, file order and exit codes. (4) Check 6 uses `gh pr view ... --json body,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup`. It requires the Closes …/issues/104 line in the body and the `test` workflow "concluded success" at the head commit.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items. Item 1: no verifier PASS/FAIL condition requires exact stderr wording. Check 3 asks only that "stderr has an error", and usage-message checks are under "Advisory (not pass/fail)". No condition sets a branch rule, a mutation test or a file-touch limit. Check 4 allows a non-empty diff as long as lint's code and behaviour are unchanged. The builder's "Do not touch src/index.js" and its suggested message wording are build instructions, not pass conditions. Check 1's "A file named twice is reported twice" follows directly from "checks every file named in order". Item 2: checks 1–3 (the behaviour lines) each run B with real files, stdin or a missing file and record stdout, stderr and exit status. None passes by reading the code. Only check 4 (not a behaviour line) uses git diff.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with each verifier check and found none of the verifier's probes in it. The builder brief has no PASS/FAIL wording and none of the verifier's concrete material: no scratch files (`$T/a.jsonl`, `{oops}`), no `printf … | B - -` pipelines, no `git diff` merge-base command and no `gh pr view` call. Its step 3 does list test cases with expected exit codes, such as "a missing file among good ones: exit 2, stderr names the missing file … include a bad file so its lines still appear". This is a borderline call because that case closely mirrors verifier Check 3's last run. I still count it as allowed. It restates what expect lines 3 and 5 require, and the criterion permits telling the builder to write its own tests. The "check before reading anything" line matches only an advisory item, not a PASS/FAIL check. The only commands the builder is told to run are `npm test` and the test workflow, which the issue names.
